finding.claim: The clone unsafe-option blocklist omits --config-env, which is equivalent to the blocked --config/-c: it sets a git config key (e.g. core.sshCommand) from an environment variable. Passing it through multi_options or kwargs bypasses the default allow_unsafe_options=False guard. Exploitation needs attacker control of both the option string and the value of the named environment variable as seen by the git subprocess (via env= or the process environment), so impact is conditional.
finding.source: Caller-supplied clone options: multi_options (a string list, shlex-split at git/repo/base.py:1528) or kwargs passed to Repo.clone_from / Repo.clone, e.g. multi_options=['--config-env=core.sshCommand=VAR'].
finding.sink: git clone subprocess invocation at git/repo/base.py:1541-1551, which runs `git clone <multi> -- <url> <path>`. git reads core.sshCommand from VAR's value and executes it on ssh transports.

trace.note: multi_options is joined and shlex-split into the `multi` token list.
Because allow_unsafe_options is False, check_unsafe_options is run on the tokenized `multi` list against unsafe_git_clone_options.
canonical_unsafe_options maps the blocklist to canonical names: upload-pack, u, config, c, template, separate-git-dir, bundle-uri.
The token '--config-env=core.sshCommand=VAR' is canonicalized by _canonicalize_option_name (cmd.py:965-977) to 'config-env'.
The prefix check tests canonical.startswith(candidate). 'config'.startswith('config-env') is False, and no other blocked name matches, so nothing is raised.
git.clone(multi, '--', ...) forwards the unchecked --config-env token to git.

finding.guards_checked: (1) allow_unsafe_protocols check on the URL (base.py:1531): not relevant, the option is not in the URL. (2) check_unsafe_options on kwargs (base.py:1533-1537): kwargs keys do not include config-env. (3) check_unsafe_options on multi tokens (base.py:1538-1539): runs but misses config-env because it only does exact, abbreviation-of-blocked-name, and short-option checks. (4) The '--' separator (base.py:1543) protects the URL and path, but not the option tokens in multi, which come before it. Not verified: whether the installed git supports --config-env (git >= 2.31 is believed to), and whether the library's test suite covers this spelling. The web search was denied, so this is from reading the code and memory of git's docs.
